harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a plain L3 router (no NAT) between lan-a (node2, eth1) and lan-b (node3, eth1), entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node4). node2 (10.50.10.10/24) and node3 (10.50.20.10/24) route through node1 (10.50.10.254 / 10.50.20.254) and reach each other directly on any port with original source addresses preserved (verified via tcpdump showing an unmodified source IP through a full TCP handshake). All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms; each showed a changed boot_id and fully recovered state (VyOS committed config persisted via `save`; Alpine static IP/route persisted via /etc/network/interfaces; a full re-run of the playbook after all restarts was 100% idempotent with connectivity re-confirmed).
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1=VyOS (eth0 mgmt, eth1/eth2 unaddressed), node2/node3=Alpine (eth0 mgmt, eth1 unaddressed/down); confirmed L2 pairing node1-eth1<->node2-eth1 (lan-a) via test ping and inferred node1-eth2<->node3-eth1 (lan-b)

Bootstrapped passwordless SSH from node4 (control node) to node1 (vyos user, passwordless sudo), node2 and node3 (root), using the cluster-provided keypair; unlocked locked root accounts on node2/node3 and installed the cluster public key for the VyOS ssh user

Wrote an Ansible project on node4 (/root/lan-routing: ansible.cfg, inventory.ini, site.yml) that (a) sets VyOS eth1/eth2 addresses via vbash configure/commit/save run through sudo to avoid nested-vbash failures, (b) bootstraps python3 and configures a persistent static-IP+route stanza in /etc/network/interfaces on node2/node3, and (c) verifies reachability
Ran the playbook; verified bidirectional ping and a raw TCP (nc) session with tcpdump on node1 confirming source-address preservation (no NAT) on a non-ping port

Captured boot_id and health baseline on all 4 nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time using each OS's native reboot mechanism, polled until each came back, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified recovered interfaces/routes/connectivity for each before moving to the next node
Re-ran the full Ansible playbook after all four restarts to confirm end-to-end idempotence and persistence of the routing configuration

evidence.requirement: node2 (lan-a) and node3 (lan-b) can reach each other directly on any port, preserving original source addresses
evidence.summary: Bidirectional ICMP ping succeeds both directions; a TCP payload sent from node2 (nc client, ephemeral port) to node3:5201 was delivered and received intact; tcpdump on node1's eth2 shows the full TCP handshake with source IP 10.50.10.10 unmodified (no NAT)

ansible-playbook site.yml run from control node4 against vyos_router and lan_hosts groups completes with all tasks ok; re-run after all node restarts is fully idempotent (changed=0 everywhere), proving the routing state is Ansible-managed and persistent

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7668189d-21f0-4471-b90b-30e7498d3d90; native systemd reboot acknowledged in background before disconnect; post-restart boot_id c504a2e8-c3df-4d24-9ef6-a5fd76496334 (changed); eth1/eth2 addresses and net.ipv4.ip_forward restored from saved VyOS config; node2->node3 ping through the router succeeds

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d828e7bd-217d-4485-8189-43e43560d698; reboot ack (exec stream closed before completion is the expected disconnect evidence of a restart in progress); post-restart boot_id 41e5f274-5c19-4a95-8a40-1f04ca355c07 (changed); eth1 static IP, static route to lan-b, and ping to node3 all recovered from persisted /etc/network/interfaces

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 282adb31-7408-4b97-92b6-f344bdd4b861; reboot ack; post-restart boot_id 170e0868-19da-4c21-b593-090df776e4c3 (changed); eth1 static IP, static route to lan-a, and ping to node2 all recovered

evidence.requirement: node4 (control node) restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id c030bd0d-0b10-4d63-8c28-fe8986003e8b; reboot ack; post-restart boot_id 59edf123-89b6-4a60-995a-0f4a33a56087 (changed); Ansible binary, cluster SSH private key, and the /root/lan-routing project all persisted across reboot; cross-LAN ping still succeeds afterward
